# An upper bound of a sum of two-limb numbers

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `add_up_2_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An upper bound of $x + y$, of two limbs, within $A\lvert x + y\rvert + B$ of it:

$$x + y \le h.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $h = h_0 + h_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`ball_to_interval_2`](ball_to_interval_2.md), [`interval_add_2`](interval_add_2.md), [`sub_up_2_2`](sub_up_2_2.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $h$ is normalized: $h_0 = \mathrm{RN}(h_0 + h_1)$.
- $h \ge x + y$, and $\lvert h - (x + y)\rvert \le A\,\lvert x + y\rvert + B$: a upper bound, moved outward from the result rounded to nearest by a bound of its error, with the constants $A$ and $B$ below; and $h = x + y$ exactly when $x + y = 0$.

The constants of the bound, from `gen/claims.json`: $A$ is `(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^3)*up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u))+2*u^2)*(1+unit(add_2_2))/(1-u)` and $B$ is `2*(1+u)^2*(1/2*up((1+u)^3)*eta+up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))+eta+(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^3)*up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u))+2*u^2)/(1-u)*tiny(add_2_2)`, where `up( )` is a constant as `T` rounds it up (the $E$, $G$, $H$ of a radius) and `unit( )`, `tiny( )` are the constants of the center's kernel; $N$ is the smallest normal number of `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| $A / u^2$ | $8.0000000000000091 \times 10^{0}$ | $8.0000048875823637 \times 10^{0}$ |
| $B / N$ | $2.0000000000000018 \times 10^{0}$ | $2.000000953674423 \times 10^{0}$ |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `add_up_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Directed2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Directed2.v), against `add_up_2_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions add_up_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition add_up_2_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let '(h0, h1) := add_up_2_2 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  normalized_2 emin prec h0 h1 /\
  ((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1)) <= (h0 + h1) /\
  Rabs ((h0 + h1) - ((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1))) <= ((((((2 * ((1 + u prec) ^ 3)) * up_ball_add_1_1 emin prec) * up_ball_add_2_0 emin prec) + (2 * (u prec ^ 2))) * (1 + ((3 / (1 - (4 * u prec))) * u prec ^ 2))) / (1 - u prec)) * Rabs ((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1)) + ((((2 * ((1 + u prec) ^ 2)) * ((((/ 2) * up_ball_add_1_1 emin prec) * eta emin) + up_ball_add_1_2 emin prec)) + eta emin) + ((((((2 * ((1 + u prec) ^ 3)) * up_ball_add_1_1 emin prec) * up_ball_add_2_0 emin prec) + (2 * (u prec ^ 2))) / (1 - u prec)) * 0)) /\
  (((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1)) = 0 -> (h0 + h1) = ((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1))).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `add_up_2_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** add_2_2 moved up by the bound of its own error, renormalized exactly (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/add_up_2_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/add_up_2_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_ball_2_2`](add_ball_2_2.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md), [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md).

```
# A normalized pair that is at least x + y: as add_down_2_2, with the second limb moved up. The
# bound is zero when the computed sum is zero, for the same reason.
# The tightness constants of the outward claim are A = (2 (1+u)^3 G E + 2 u^2) (1 + rel) / (1 - u)
# and B = 2 (1+u)^2 (G eta / 2 + H) + eta + (2 (1+u)^3 G E + 2 u^2) / (1 - u) tiny, with E, G, H the
# constants of the radius as the format rounds them, and rel, tiny those of the bound of the
# center's kernel (milestone2.md, "Bounds of two limbs"; Directed2.v, outward_rel, outward_abs).

(z0, z1, d) = add_ball_2_2(x0, x1, y0, y1)
zd          = eq(z0, 0)
dd          = select(zd, 0, d)
w           = add_up_1(z1, dd)
(h0, h1)    = two_sum_ord(z0, w)
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: [`ball_to_interval_2`](ball_to_interval_2.md) and [`interval_add_2`](interval_add_2.md) states that ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values) says what the library does now).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
